entries.task_title: Week 1: measure his threshold distance and write the number down
entries.evidence: WHAT TO DO: on a few walks, note the distance at which he FIRST fixates on another dog, and the distance at which he STARTS BARKING. Record both in feet.
entries.matched: Week 1: measure his threshold distance and write the number down

entries.task_title: Week 1: re-route and re-time walks so he stops rehearsing the barking
entries.evidence: For the next 1–2 weeks, deliberately pick walks where you will NOT meet dogs at close range: earlier morning or later evening, quiet residential or light-industrial streets, school grounds outside hours, wide-open space where you can see dogs coming from 100 ft.
entries.matched: Week 1: re-route and re-time walks so he stops rehearsing the barking

entries.task_title: Week 2: run Engage/Disengage Level 1 — do not close the distance yet
entries.evidence:

entries.matched: Week 2: run Engage/Disengage Level 1 — do not close the distance yet

entries.task_title: Week 3: move to Level 2 (disengage) and start closing distance in steps
entries.evidence: After 3–5 clean reps in a row, move 1–5 STEPS closer. Steps, not yards.
entries.matched: Week 3: move to Level 2 (disengage) and start closing distance in steps

entries.task_title: Week 4: generalise across different dogs, then rehearse the real-world pass
entries.evidence: 1. GENERALISE. Repeat the whole procedure with DIFFERENT dogs — big, small, fluffy, barky, calm.

handoffs.evidence: Email DogTraining@hssv.org with proof of adoption (where and when you adopted him) and ask for the adopter access code, plus which classes it applies to.

handoffs.task_title: Buy the equipment before Week 1 starts
handoffs.evidence: - Front-clip harness, fitted. This is the main anti-pulling tool — it takes pressure off his neck and turns him rather than letting him lean into it.

handoffs.task_title: Week 1: measure his threshold distance and write the number down
handoffs.evidence: WHAT TO DO: on a few walks, note the distance at which he FIRST fixates on another dog, and the distance at which he STARTS BARKING. Record both in feet.

handoffs.task_title: Week 1: re-route and re-time walks so he stops rehearsing the barking
handoffs.evidence: For the next 1–2 weeks, deliberately pick walks where you will NOT meet dogs at close range: earlier morning or later evening, quiet residential or light-industrial streets, school grounds outside hours, wide-open space where you can see dogs coming from 100 ft.

handoffs.task_title: Week 2: run Engage/Disengage Level 1 — do not close the distance yet
handoffs.evidence:
1. The instant he LOOKS at the other dog: CLICK.
2. When he turns his head back to you after the click: FEED.

handoffs.task_title: Week 3: move to Level 2 (disengage) and start closing distance in steps
handoffs.evidence: After 3–5 clean reps in a row, move 1–5 STEPS closer. Steps, not yards.

handoffs.task_title: Week 4: generalise across different dogs, then rehearse the real-world pass
handoffs.evidence: 1. GENERALISE. Repeat the whole procedure with DIFFERENT dogs — big, small, fluffy, barky, calm.
